hypothesis: The parent disabled CTS sink clustering entirely (size/diameter = 0), which improved TNS but degraded WNS. A middle ground — restore a modest sink-cluster size/diameter (smaller than the baseline's 30/100 but non-zero, e.g. 10/50) — should keep the TNS benefit of less aggressive clustering while recovering the WNS loss by giving CTS enough grouping to build a shorter, more balanced clock tree, reducing propagated-clock setup violations across all circuits.
analysis: Crash failure (KeyError in partition) on bp_fe-ng45/1002; only one seed listed, so likely sporadic but unconfirmed—invalid run says nothing about the hypothesis. Among valid runs, hypothesis partly holds: ariane133 and bp show WNS/TNS gains, but bp_fe shows WNS +4.8% yet TNS −24.8%, contradicting the "keep TNS benefit" claim. Mechanism: modest clustering helps clock balance (WNS) but bp_fe's TNS regresses, possibly from residual skew/setup paths. Next step: fix the partition KeyError (guard missing partition keys) and rerun all seeds to confirm whether bp_fe TNS loss is real before tuning size/diameter.
